Purpose
Previous dynamic prediction models rarely handle multi-period data with different intervals, and the large-scale patient hospital records are not effectively used to improve the prediction performance. This paper aims to focus on the prediction of cardiovascular disease using the improved long short-term memory (LSTM) model.


Design/methodology/approach
A new model based on the traditional LSTM was proposed to predict cardiovascular disease. The irregular time interval is smoothed to obtain the time parameter vector, and it is used as the input of the forgetting gate of LSTM to overcome the prediction obstacle caused by the irregular time interval.


Findings
The experimental results show that the dynamic prediction model proposed in this paper obtained a significant better classification performance compared with the traditional LSTM model.


Originality/value
In this paper, the authors improved the LSTM by smoothing the irregular time between different medical stages of the patient to obtain the temporal feature vector.

Purpose
Earlier dynamic prediction models seldom cope with multi-period data at varying intervals, and large-scale patient hospital records are not effectively leveraged to improve prediction performance. This paper focuses on predicting cardiovascular disease with an improved long short-term memory (LSTM) model.

Design/methodology/approach
A novel model built on the conventional LSTM was proposed for cardiovascular disease prediction. Irregular time intervals are smoothed to derive a time parameter vector, which is then fed into the LSTM forgetting gate to overcome the prediction difficulty caused by irregular intervals.

Findings
Experimental results indicate that the dynamic prediction model presented in this paper achieved significantly better classification performance than the traditional LSTM model.

Originality/value
The authors enhanced the LSTM by smoothing the irregular time between different medical stages of the patient to obtain a temporal feature vector.
